hook.text: Ancient Rome had a vast road network—and travelers needed somewhere to sleep. Roadside inns were the answer.

buildup.text: Called 'cauponae,' these inns offered beds, food, and stables. Most were simple, noisy, and often dangerous.

discovery.text: Wealthy Romans avoided them entirely. They stayed at private villas of friends—public inns were for commoners.

twist.text: Innkeepers had terrible reputations. Roman law actually held them liable if guests were robbed or murdered.

climax.text: Despite the bad reputation, these inns made long-distance travel possible across the entire Roman Empire.

punchline.text: Cheap beds, bad reputations, big impact. Hotels started rough.
